'''''Vandenboschia speciosa''''', [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]] '''''Trichomanes speciosum''''',<ref name=CFLW/> commonly known as the '''Killarney fern''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=17 October 2014 }}</ref>  is a species of [[fern]] found widely in [[Western Europe]]. It is most abundant in [[Ireland]], [[Great Britain]], [[Brittany]], [[Galicia (Spain)|Galicia]], [[Canary Islands]], [[Madeira]] and the [[Azores]], but is also found in other locations including [[France]], [[Spain]], [[Portugal]] and [[Italy]].<ref>[http://www.ukbap.org.uk/UKPlans.aspx?ID=615 "Species Action Plan: Killarney Fern (''Trichomanes speciosum'')"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110201222726/http://www.ukbap.org.uk/UKPlans.aspx?ID=615 |date=2011-02-01 }} BAP. Retrieved 26 June 2008.</ref> It is a relict endemic European species with a disjunct distribution, having had a much wider distribution before the climate changes of the [[Tertiary period|Tertiary]] and [[Quaternary]] periods.<ref name=Schuler>{{cite journal |author=Schuler, Samira Ben-Menni  |author2=García-López, María del Carmen |author3=López-Flores, Inmaculada |author4=Nieto-Lugilde, Marta |author5=Suárez-Santiago, Víctor N. |year=2016 |title=Genetic diversity and population history of the Killarney fern, ''Vandenboschia speciosa'' (Hymenophyllaceae), at its southern distribution limit in continental Europe |journal=Botanical Journal of the Linnean Society |volume=183 |issue=1 |pages=94–105 |doi=10.1111/boj.12492 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

This fern has an unusual life cycle, with a perennial gametophyte phase with an active vegetative reproduction. The gametophyte has the ability to tolerate darker and drier habitats than does the sporophyte.<ref name=Schuler/> The [[sporophyte]] form is found in only 16 locations in the UK although the [[gametophyte]] form is more widespread. Once found on [[Isle of Arran|Arran]], it was thought to be extinct in [[Scotland]] due to the activities of [[Pteridomania|Victorian collectors]],<ref>Ratcliffe, Derek (1977) ''Highland Flora''. Inverness. HIDB. page 40.</ref> but the species has been discovered on [[Skye]] in its gametophyte form.<ref>[http://www.plant-identification.co.uk/skye/index.htm "Skye Flora"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090208104307/http://plant-identification.co.uk/skye/index.htm |date=2009-02-08 }}. plant-identification.co.uk. Retrieved 25 May 2008.</ref> In the UK it is classed as [[Vulnerable species|vulnerable]] and it is considered one of Europe's most threatened plants.<ref>[http://www.english-nature.org.uk/science/srp/rare_ferns.htm "Species Recovery Programme"] English Nature. Retrieved 26 June 2008.</ref> It is found mostly near the western coasts of the United Kingdom and Ireland and at scattered locations inland.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/plant/poa-nemoralis |title=''Poa nemoralis'' |work=Online Atlas of the British and Irish Flora |access-date=8 March 2020 |archive-date=12 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200812063627/https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/plant/poa-nemoralis }}</ref>

Killarney fern is a medium-sized, long-lived fern with delicate, highly divided, bipinnate fronds arising from a creeping rhizome.<ref name=JNCC>{{cite web |url=https://sac.jncc.gov.uk/species/S1421/ |title=Killarney fern ''Trichomanes speciosum'' |publisher=JNCC |access-date=8 March 2020}}</ref>  It is one of only three European species with translucent leaves and requires a humid, frost-free environment. In Britain, it is largely restricted to damp, shady, sheltered locations such as ravines,<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120721035551/http://www.arkive.org/species/ARK/plants_and_algae/Trichomanes_speciosum/more_info.html?section=description|title="Killarney fern  (Trichomanes speciosum)"}} Arkive.  Retrieved 26 June 2008.</ref> although in Ireland it occupies a wider range of habitats. In Brittany, it grows on the stonework of a number of ancient wells.<ref name=JNCC/>

It became a protected species in the UK in 1975 under the Conservation of Wild Creatures and Wild Plants Act.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.caithness.org/caithnessfieldclub/bulletins/1975/october/conservation.htm |title=Conservation of Wild Creatures and Wild Plants Act |author=Butler, K. |work=Caithness Field Club Bulletin |access-date=8 March 2020}}</ref>
